forecasts.reason: No recipe change: the 0-2 seed numbers reproduce bit-identically. The 10-seed mean is most likely within 0.3 pp of 0.7548, with a seed std of 0.2-0.3 pp.
With 100 classes, label smoothing 0.3 vs 0.2 changes the target entropy only modestly, and the EMA already smooths the result. The likely gap is about 0.1-0.2 pp, below the 0.3 pp threshold.
Weights are renormalized each step, so the Muon lr sets the angular step size. A ×1.5 lr adds late-phase noise that the EMA only partly absorbs. Probably neutral to slightly negative.
Muon has no weight-decay term and the conv weights are norm-fixed, so wd only acts on the BN biases, whitening bias and head. Expect a near-null effect.
The code already runs 3 Newton-Schulz steps (the default steps=3), so the change is a no-op. Accuracy should be identical and time within noise.

At about 26 ms per step the GPU is saturated, and the eager SGD/Lookahead foreach ops and Python LR fills cause no syncs. Expect a saving below 3%. Moving augmentation into the compiled region may also shift the RNG stream and so the accuracy.
Lookahead's reset also anneals the fast weights. A plain EMA with a horizon of about 20 steps keeps the averaging but loses the reset. Expect about −0.2 pp, close to the 0.3 pp tolerance.

cruxes: Is the tip's train step fully GPU-bound, or do launch gaps exist under the 4-CPU pin? This decides whether I021 or CUDA graphs can give a 3% or larger time cut.
Do seeds 0-2 sit above or below the held-out seed mean (I016)? With a 0.18 pp margin, this decides whether time must be spent to buy margin or epochs can keep being cut.
Is Lookahead's benefit mostly the reset (an annealing effect) or endpoint averaging (I022)? The answer says which time-neutral accuracy levers remain.
structured_output.world_model: W1 (mechanism), after E010. The run is GPU/FLOP-bound: time scales with pixel share × width FLOPs, plus about 0.4 s of fixed cost. Every FLOP lever costs about 0.4-0.5 pp per 10% of time. The tip margin is 0.18 pp. Muon renormalizes the conv filters every step, so weight decay only acts on the BN biases, whitening bias and head, and the Muon lr is an angular step size. Newton-Schulz already runs 3 steps (the default), so I020 is a no-op. Lookahead's resets anneal the fast weights, and a plain EMA probably loses about 0.2 pp. Time-neutral accuracy levers (label smoothing, lr, wd) look like at most ±0.2 pp, which 3 seeds cannot resolve. Graph-break or launch fixes are worth 0-3% of time.
